items.title: Megan’s Family Restaurant
items.html:
Facebook: Megan’s Family Restaurant

Phone: (218) 229-3418
Address: 114 N Main Street, Aurora, MN 55705

A cozy, hometown diner in downtown Aurora serving American comfort classics in a low-key, family-style setting. Perfect for an early breakfast (try the Hungry Man platter or biscuits & gravy) or a casual lunch: burgers, sandwiches, homemade soups and classic entrees. Friendly staff, affordable prices, and a true Iron Range atmosphere. Opens at 7 AM; closed Mondays; open later on Fridays for the fish fry. Check Facebook or call for current hours. Ideal for fueling up before exploring the parks!

A cozy clubhouse restaurant with breathtaking views of the Quarry golf course and cliff-edged lakes. Open daily from sunrise to sunset during the golf season (roughly late spring through mid-fall), it serves full-service breakfast, lunch, dinner, and a full bar. Ideal for a scenic morning pancake/brunch, afternoon bite, or relaxed evening meal after your outdoor adventures. Closed in winter; check the website for opening dates.

items.title: Dining Specials: Rotating Chophouse Menu
items.html:
The Chophouse Menu is a monthly rotating dinner menu served at Burnt Onion Kitchen & Brews in the Giants Ridge Chalet, starting at 4 PM on days the restaurant is open. Enjoy succulent steaks, grilled chops, savory sides, and decadent desserts, all designed to deliver a memorable gourmet experience.

Pair your meal with a curated selection of brews and wines for the perfect evening at Giants Ridge.

Burnt Onion closes between seasons in late fall and reopens for ski season (scheduled for Nov. 28); check current hours before you go.

Current menu and details: giantsridge.com/fb-specials

items.title: Burnt Onion Kitchen & Brews
items.html:

Phone: (218) 865-8061
Location: 2nd floor of the Main Chalet at Giants Ridge, 6329 Wynne Creek Drive, Biwabik

This lodge-style eatery offers creative American cuisine with local flair. Try the signature Burnt Onion Burger, enjoy fresh walleye, or savor vegetarian/gluten-free choices. After a day of skiing, biking, or hiking, unwind on the deck overlooking the slopes with a craft beer, cocktail or mocktail in hand. Wheelchair accessible via the first-floor elevator.

Hours are seasonal: summer 2026 was Thursday-Sunday from 11 AM; the restaurant closes between seasons in fall and reopens for ski season (scheduled for Nov. 28). Check the website for current hours.

items.title: The Legend
items.html:
giantsridge.com/the-legend

Golf Shop: (218) 865-8030 · Resort toll-free: (800) 688-7669

A premium 18-hole, par-72 public course set in the heart of mature red-pine forest. Designed by Jeff Brauer and Lanny Wadkins, it challenges golfers of all levels with dynamic terrain, pristine bent-grass greens, and stunning natural beauty.

Rated as one of Minnesota’s best public courses, it offers full-service amenities—driving range, pro shop, club rental, lessons, and clubhouse dining. Book your tee time online via Giants Ridge or GolfNow, and browse hole maps and scorecards to prepare. Perfect for a memorable “nine-and-dine” or full round experience during your stay.

Season: The 2026 golf season ended Oct. 11, 2026. The 2027 opening date has not been announced yet; check the course page in spring.

items.title: The Quarry
items.html:
giantsridge.com/the-quarry

Golf Shop: (218) 865-8030 · Main line: (218) 865-8000 · Resort toll-free: (800) 688-7669

A premier 18-hole, par-72 public course carved from historic mine terrain, offering rugged beauty and strategic play. Designed by Jeff Brauer, it’s challenging (7,201 yards, slope up to 146) with elevation, rock formations, and standout holes like the drivable 13th. Golf Digest (2025) ranks it the top Minnesota course on its list of America’s 100 Greatest Public Courses (No. 58 nationally)—a must for enthusiastic golfers.

Season: The 2026 golf season ended Oct. 11, 2026. The 2027 opening date has not been announced yet.

items.title: Weddings & Banquets

Plan Your Dream Wedding or Special Event at Giants Ridge
Celebrate your special day surrounded by the natural beauty of Northern Minnesota. Giants Ridge offers stunning indoor and outdoor venues, expert coordination, and full-service banquet options to ensure your event is seamless and unforgettable.

Ceremony Locations:

items.title: Pool & Sauna Haus
items.html:
Check out the Pool & Sauna Haus at Giants Ridge!

Open to the public and just 5 minutes from our home, it offers a heated indoor pool, an expansive hot tub, and two dry saunas (add steam with the provided buckets and ladles) for year-round relaxation.

Conveniently located across from the main entrance, the Pool & Sauna Haus offers forest views, a cozy lobby fireplace, and a warm, inviting atmosphere—an ideal spot to relax after a day of adventure. Resort guests, day visitors, and community members are welcome; anyone under 18 must be supervised by an adult.

Hours: Open swim daily, 6:00 AM – 8:00 PM. Morning relaxation & lap swim 6:00 – 10:00 AM.

Rates

  • Monthly pass: $75
  • Winter alpine season pass holders: 25% off daily passes

Party Room Rental

  • $175 for 3 hours, includes up to 10 swim passes for the same block
  • Catering menu available; no outside food or drink except cake or cupcakes

items.title: The Legend Golf Course
items.html:
Scenic. Challenging. Legendary.
Opened in 1997, The Legend has become one of Minnesota’s most celebrated public golf courses. Recognized by Golf Digest as one of the “Top 10 Best New Upscale Public Courses in the Nation,” this award-winning course offers a serene, unforgettable experience with unmatched value. More recently, Golfweek ranked it among the Best Resort Courses in the U.S. (No. 105, 2026).

Nestled in the scenic Iron Range, The Legend helped establish Northern Minnesota as a global golf destination.

2026 Green Fees (last season; 2027 rates not yet posted; include cart & range balls, plus tax/fees)

  • Early (opening – May 28): $100
  • Prime (May 29 – Aug 23): $130 | Twilight $100 after 3 PM | Same-day replay $75
  • Fall (Aug 24 – Sept 27): $130 | Twilight $100 after 2 PM
  • Late (Sept 28 – Oct 11): $100 | Same-day replay $75
  • Junior (17 & under): $45 all season

Special Deal: 36-Hole Experience
Play both The Legend and The Quarry on the same day with lunch in between. Available during prime season only (May 29 – Aug 23 in 2026). Call ahead to book both tee times.

Season: The 2026 season ended Oct. 11; 2027 dates TBA.

Learn more or book your tee time: giantsridge.com/the-legend

items.title: The Quarry Golf Course
items.html:
Minnesota’s No. 1 Public Golf Course

Built on the site of a former sand, gravel, and iron ore mine, The Quarry offers a rugged, dramatic, and unforgettable golfing experience. Golf Digest (2025) ranks it the top Minnesota course on its list of America’s 100 Greatest Public Courses (No. 58 nationally), and Golfweek has rated it No. 1 among Minnesota public courses. A perfect complement to the more traditional Legend course.

items.title: Climbing Wall
items.html:
Experience climbing on the A.R.T.Wall™, a unique 32-foot-tall, four-sided concrete wall modeled from real rock for an incredibly realistic climb. Its solid, cool-to-the-touch surface offers an authentic and safe climbing experience, with auto-belays on most routes.

Climbers must be at least 5 years old, 40 lbs, and 42 inches tall. All climbers sign a waiver; minors (17 and under) need a parent or guardian to sign. Children under 14 must be supervised by an adult.

Hours: Fridays through Sundays during the summer season.
Rates (last posted): Day pass $14; shoe rental $4; chalk bag $4. Passes are sold at the Main Chalet gift shop (first floor).

More info: giantsridge.com/climbing-wall

items.title: Disc Golf
items.html:
Play one of Minnesota’s most scenic and longest disc golf courses, spanning 80+ acres and up to 10,000 feet in fairway distance. The 18-hole mountain course features dual concrete tees, multiple pin placements, and challenging terrain with grassy hills, woods, and rocks.

Average playtime: 2.5 hours.
Wear sturdy footwear suitable for hiking-style terrain.

More info: https://www.giantsridge.com/disc-golf/

items.html:
Explore a variety of trails for all skill levels:

  • Wynne Lake Vista Trail: Moderate, 0.8-mile loop
  • Northface Trail: Difficult, 1.1 miles one way

items.title: Mountain Biking
items.html:
Mountain Biking at Giants Ridge

Giants Ridge offers over 9 miles of purpose-built cross-country trails through the Superior National Forest, ideal for all levels of riders. For more thrill, ride the Sarajevo Express chairlift to 12 gravity trails featuring berms, jumps, and rugged terrain—from beginner-friendly green to double black diamond.

A valid pass is required. Full-face helmets are highly recommended on all gravity trails.

Season: Lift-served biking runs late May through mid-October; the 2026 bike park season is over and 2027 dates have not been announced.
Last posted day tickets (gravity): Adult (13+) $42 online / $47 in person; Child (7–12) $32 online / $35 in person. XC-only day pass $6.

More info and trail map: giantsridge.com/mountain-biking

items.title: Scenic Chairlift Rides
items.html:
Take in stunning views of the Superior National Forest with a relaxing ride on the Sarajevo Express, Giants Ridge’s high-speed quad chairlift. At the top, enjoy breathtaking vistas of the Iron Range—an unforgettable way to experience the beauty of the mountain, especially during fall colors.

Season: Summer and fall weekends (2026 fall rides ran Fri–Sun in September and Sat–Sun in October, 10 AM – 5/6 PM; last ride up one hour before close). Closed for the 2026 season.
Last posted rates: Adult $10, Child $5.

More info: giantsridge.com/scenic-chairlift-rides

items.title: Children's Play Area
items.html:
Location: Tucked between the Main Chalet and The Lodge at Giants Ridge, this play area is conveniently located near the heart of the resort.

A delightful space where children can burn off energy and enjoy fresh air in the Northwoods. Features include:

  • Multiple slides with varying routes and heights
  • Fun climbing obstacles built for kids
  • Signage with regional outdoor adventure info

Ideal for families—while the kids play, you can plan your next mountain biking trail, golf round, or lakeside adventure.

Good to know

  • Unsupervised: The play space is not monitored. Please keep an eye on children at all times.
  • Seasonal: Open as the seasons allow (generally the snow-free months).
  • Easy to reach from the Mountain Sports Shop, restaurants, and trailheads.

More info: giantsridge.com/explore

items.title: Giants Ridge Bike Park Trail Map
items.html:
Discover Northern Minnesota’s Premier Mountain Biking Destination

Welcome to Giants Ridge Bike Park, where rugged terrain, scenic views, and thrilling trails converge to offer one of the most diverse biking experiences in the Midwest. Whether you're a beginner, a gravity-fueled adventurer, or a cross-country explorer, there's a trail waiting for you here. Follow the “Pre-Ride, Re-Ride, Free-Ride” safety model to get the most out of your day.

Full Trail Map (PDF): Giants Ridge Bike Park Map
Current trail conditions: Trailforks – Giants Ridge

Trail lengths below are from the printed map; the resort’s website lists some updated gravity-trail lengths.

Gravity Freeride (lift-accessed jumps, berms, and flow)

  • Ribbit One, Two, Three – about 0.28 mi each | Intro trails with berms and smooth rolls
  • Tadpole – 1.0 mi | Beginner-friendly flow
  • Leapfrog – 1.0 mi | Great transitions and moderate features
  • Featherlys – 0.74 mi | Smooth and flowy, intermediate
  • Return to Send’er – 0.85 mi | Intermediate flow

items.title: Winter Equipment Rentals
items.html:
Rent everything you need for a day on the slopes—from skis and snowboards to snowshoes and fat tire bikes. All downhill packages include a helmet and are fitted by certified rental technicians.

Rental Options Include:

  • Alpine & Snowboard Gear

  • Nordic Ski Equipment

  • Snowshoes

  • Fat Tire Bikes

Ski & Snowboard Rental Pricing:
Includes skis/snowboard, boots, poles, and helmet

  • Adult (13+): $39

  • Youth (7–12): $29

  • Child (6 & under): $14

  • High-performance package: $53 (Adult)

Add-Ons & A La Carte Options:

  • Skis/Board only: $32 (Adult), $21 (Youth)

  • Boots: $18 (Adult), $14 (Youth), $12 (Child)

Booking Info:
Please purchase rentals and lift tickets online in advance. After checkout, waivers will be sent to your email—complete them before your visit. Pick up lift tickets at the desk before heading to rentals.

Other rentals: Nordic waxless package $18 (Adult) / $12 (Child); snowshoes $14/day; fat tire bikes $40 per session (9 AM–12 PM or 1–4 PM).

Note: Rentals are first come, first served and subject to availability. Winter opening day is announced as Nov. 27, 2026 (weather permitting).

More info: https://www.giantsridge.com/equipment-rentals/

items.title: Giants Ridge Winter Trail Map
items.html:
Explore Giants Ridge with ease using the winter trail map. It shows 35 alpine runs served by five chairlifts (Sarajevo Express, Calgary, Helsinki, Chamonix, and Rocky Top) plus conveyor and tow lifts, along with the snow tubing park, Nordic and snowshoe trails, fat-bike routes, and resort buildings including the Pool & Sauna Haus.

Trail & ski map: Giants Ridge Alpine Trail Map
Snowshoe map: Snowshoe Trail Map (PDF)

items.title: Skiing & Snowboarding
items.html:
Hit the slopes at Giants Ridge for an unforgettable winter adventure. With 35 well-groomed runs for all skill levels, top-quality ski and snowboard rentals, and affordable daily tickets and season passes, it’s the perfect spot for beginners and seasoned pros alike.

Everything you need for a great day on the mountain is right here.

Season: Winter opening day is announced as Nov. 27, 2026 (weather permitting); closing date depends on conditions.

2026–27 highlights:

  • Kids 12 and under ski and ride free all season (proof of age required; kids get a media card on their first visit)
  • Thursday Night Lights: free skiing 4–8 PM on Thursdays, starting Dec. 31

Buy lift tickets and rentals online in advance. Daily lift ticket prices are listed on the Giants Ridge online shop.

More info: giantsridge.com/skiing-snowboarding
Lift tickets & season passes: giantsridge.com/winter-season-passes

items.title: Nordic Skiing
items.html:
Giants Ridge is a premier Nordic skiing destination with a rich history—its trail system once served as a training ground for the U.S. Ski Team. Today, skiers of all ages and skill levels can explore miles of scenic trails through the Superior National Forest, with options ranging from green to black, including the lighted Northern Light trail (lights off at 8 PM).

Whether you're out for a peaceful glide or a serious workout, you’ll find the perfect trail here.

Trail passes (2025–26 rates; 2026–27 not yet posted): Full day $18 adult / $10 child; night $11 adult / $10 child. Waxless rental package $18 adult / $12 child.

More info: giantsridge.com/cross-country-skiing

items.title: Snow Tubing
items.html:
Snow tubing is a must-try winter activity that's fun for all ages—no experience needed! Glide down one of three tubing lanes, then ride the handle tow back up for more. It’s an easy, exciting way to enjoy the snow with family and friends.

Hours (2025–26 schedule): Saturdays, 10:00 AM – 4:45 PM. Check the website for the 2026–27 schedule.
Riders must be at least 5 years old and 42 inches tall. Snow boots required (no ski boots). Tickets must be bought online in advance.

More info: giantsridge.com/snow-tubing

items.title: Snowshoeing
items.html:
Explore the quiet beauty of winter on about 3.6 miles of scenic snowshoe trails. Wander through peaceful Northwoods landscapes along the Sleeping Giant (1.1 mi), North Face (1.2 mi), and Narrows (1.3 mi) trails—some even wrapping around Wynne Lake.

A great way to enjoy the outdoors at a slower pace, surrounded by the natural beauty of the Superior National Forest. Snowshoe rentals are $14 per day at the rental shop.

Snowshoe map: Snowshoe Trail Map (PDF)
More info: giantsridge.com/snowshoeing

items.title: Fat Tire Biking
items.html:
Giants Ridge is a pioneer in Minnesota’s fat tire biking scene. Ride groomed winter trails including the North XC Loop, Norway, Miner’s Mile, and designated Nordic trails, or take on lift-served fat biking on gravity trails like Tadpole, Ribbits, Leapfrog, and Kitty Cat.

With routes winding through the scenic Superior National Forest, this is winter biking at its best. Use purpose-built fat bikes only (tires 3.7″ or wider, 10 psi or less), yield to skiers, and stay out of classic ski tracks.

Last posted rates: Lift & trail pass $32 (lift-served passes sold online only); trail pass only $18; fat bike rental $40 per session (9 AM – 12 PM or 1 – 4 PM, limited to 8 riders).

More info: giantsridge.com/fat-tire-biking
